goals.title: Set up DeepSeek locally on M1 Pro
goals.description:
## Overview
Configure and run DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B locally using Ollama or Transformers on M1 Pro Mac. Goal is to achieve 8-15 tokens/sec with 4-bit quantization for efficient local code generation.

**Integration Tag:** local_llm_setup
**Duration:** 3–5 days
**Career Impact:** Local AI development capability, reduced cloud dependency

## Action Tracks

### Track 1: Environment Setup (Day 1)
- Install Ollama on macOS (brew install ollama)
- Verify Metal GPU support for M1 Pro
- Install Python dependencies: transformers, torch, accelerate
- Configure environment variables for optimal performance

### Track 2: Model Installation & Configuration (Day 2)
- Pull DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B model via Ollama
- Test basic inference with sample code prompts
- Configure 4-bit quantization settings
- Benchmark initial tokens/sec performance

### Track 3: Performance Optimization (Days 3–4)
- Adjust batch size and context window
- Fine-tune memory allocation for M1 architecture
- Test different quantization levels (4-bit vs 8-bit)
- Profile GPU memory usage and thermal performance

### Track 4: Integration & Testing (Day 5)
- Create Python wrapper for easy API access
- Test with real code generation tasks (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript)
- Compare output quality vs. cloud models
- Document setup process and performance metrics

## Performance Targets
- **Throughput:** 8–15 tokens/sec
- **Memory Usage:** <8GB RAM
- **Latency:** <500ms for first token
- **Quality:** Code completion accuracy >85%

## Reflection Prompts
- What performance trade-offs exist between quantization levels?
- How does local LLM performance compare to cloud APIs?
- What use cases benefit most from local deployment?

## Output Artifacts
- Setup documentation
- Performance benchmarks
- Integration scripts
- Integration: /tools/local_llm

goals.title: Master AI Systems Design & Orchestration
goals.description:
## Overview
Develop deep expertise in AI architecture, multi-agent orchestration, and reusable design patterns. Build AI Orchestrator v2 with advanced routing, memory management, and context-awareness.

**Integration Tag:** ai_systems_design
**Duration:** 10–12 weeks
**Career Impact:** AI Solutions Architect readiness

## Action Tracks

### Track 1: Architecture Foundations (Weeks 1–3)
- Review existing AI Orchestrator v1 architecture
- Identify limitations in routing, memory, and context management
- Draft modular architecture blueprint for v2 (core + agents + API layers)
- Document architectural decisions (ADR format)

### Track 2: Build Reusable Patterns (Weeks 4–8)
- Implement 3 reusable orchestration templates:
  • context-aware-routing
  • multi-agent-coordination
  • reflection-generation-loop
- Validate each via small proof-of-concepts
- Package + publish to internal library or GitHub repo

### Track 3: Deploy & Evaluate (Weeks 9–12)
- Integrate orchestration templates into AI Orchestrator v2
- Conduct stress tests using multiple LLMs
- Create final design report + architecture diagrams

## Reflection Prompts
- What new orchestration principles emerged from hands-on builds?
- How did context-awareness improve model routing quality?

## Output Artifacts

- Architecture documentation
- Integration: /growth/projects, /growth/designs

goals.title: AI Orchestrator Architecture Enhancements
goals.description:
## Overview
Implement high-priority architecture improvements for performance, reliability, and scalability. Focus on production-ready features including caching, rate limiting, circuit breakers, and enhanced observability.

**Integration Tag:** architecture_enhancements
**Duration:** 4–6 weeks
**Career Impact:** Production system design expertise, operational excellence

## Action Tracks

### Track 1: Performance Optimization (Weeks 1–2)
- Implement semantic caching layer with Redis
- Add request deduplication for identical queries
- Optimize context window management
- Profile and reduce latency bottlenecks
- Add connection pooling for database operations

### Track 2: Reliability & Resilience (Weeks 2–3)
- Implement circuit breaker pattern for LLM providers
- Add automatic failover and retry logic
- Configure rate limiting per provider (token bucket algorithm)
- Add health check endpoints for all dependencies
- Implement graceful degradation strategies

### Track 3: Observability & Monitoring (Week 4)
- Expand Prometheus metrics coverage
- Add structured logging with correlation IDs
- Create Grafana dashboards for SLI/SLO tracking
- Implement distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry
- Set up alerting rules for critical failures

### Track 4: Scalability & Testing (Weeks 5–6)
- Add horizontal scaling support (stateless design)
- Implement request queuing for load management
- Conduct load testing (100+ concurrent requests)
- Create performance regression test suite
- Document architecture decisions and trade-offs

## Success Metrics
- **Cache Hit Rate:** >40%
- **P95 Latency:** <2s for cached requests
- **Availability:** >99.5% uptime
- **Failure Recovery:** <5s automatic failover
- **Throughput:** Handle 50+ req/min sustained

## Key Enhancements
- Semantic caching with embedding similarity
- Multi-level circuit breakers
- Adaptive rate limiting
- Comprehensive observability stack
- Auto-scaling capabilities

## Reflection Prompts
- Which architectural patterns had the biggest impact on reliability?
- How did caching affect user experience and cost?
- What observability gaps still exist?

## Output Artifacts
- Architecture decision records (ADRs)
- Performance benchmark reports
- Runbook for operations
- Integration: /growth/architecture, /metrics/performance

goals.title: Centralized monitoring for all services
goals.description:
🆕 **Add New Initiative: Centralized Observability & Performance Hub**

**Category:** Systems Architecture / Observability  
**Linked Projects:** AI Orchestrator, eCommerce Platform, Recipe Tracker  
**Integration Type:** Cross-Project Enhancement  

---

### 🧠 Initiative Overview
Establish a **Centralized Observability & Performance Hub** to unify monitoring, metrics, and tracing across all projects.  
This hub will consolidate Prometheus, Grafana, Tempo, and Loki setups into one shared telemetry layer, enabling cost, performance, and reliability visibility organization-wide.

**Objective:**  
Create a unified platform for performance analytics, cross-project comparisons, and automated reflection triggers via `metrics_agent`.

---

### 🎯 Key Goals
1. **Infrastructure Unification**
   - Deploy shared Prometheus + Grafana + Tempo + Loki stack  
   - Configure central OpenTelemetry Collector endpoint  
   - Standardize data ingestion format for all projects  

2. **Cross-Project Instrumentation**
   - Implement lightweight telemetry adapters in each project  
   - Normalize metrics naming (latency, cost, errors)  
   - Enable trace correlation between services  

3. **Dashboard & Visualization**
   - Build Grafana dashboards: system overview, cost tracker, trace explorer  
   - Integrate enhancement impact metrics  
   - Configure alerts and anomaly detection rules  

4. **AI Integration**
   - Feed metrics to `metrics_agent` for autonomous insights  
   - Link improvement deltas to enhancement IDs  
   - Trigger reflection updates in Self Development Tracker  

---

### ⏱ Estimated Effort
| Phase | Description | Duration |
|--------|-------------|-----------|
| Phase 1 | Setup central observability stack | 1–2 days |
| Phase 2 | Instrumentation (Orchestrator + eCommerce) | 2–3 days |
| Phase 3 | Metrics-to-reflection automation | 1–2 days |
| **Total** | **1 week** | |

---

### 🧩 Impact Metrics
- Reduce per-project monitoring maintenance overhead by **>50%**  
- Enable **real-time performance comparison** across projects  
- Create **automated reflection triggers** tied to performance outcomes  

---

### 📘 Reflection Mapping

- **Reflection Prompt:**  
  “What patterns emerged across projects after integrating the unified observability stack?  
  How did this centralization improve my architectural decision-making and ability to manage performance holistically?”

goals.title: AI Orchestrator Architecture & LLM Expansion
goals.description:
## Overview
Integrate vLLM (production), Llama3 (dev/code), maintain Ollama/Llama2 (logs), add ConversationState manager, plugin-based Provider & Tool Registry, centralized SRE Analytics, and pydantic config validation.

**Priority:** P0
**Target Date:** 2025-11-19

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 0 — Prep (1 day)
- Add routing_weights.yaml and providers_dev.yaml
- Add pydantic config models (basic)
- Add request trace_id injection middleware
- Add central Prometheus scrape config placeholder

### Phase 1 — vLLM Integration (3 days)
- Implement src/providers/vllm_provider.py
- Add vLLM config to config/config.yaml
- Update LocalLLMService to support provider: vllm|ollama
- Add Docker Compose service for vLLM (GPU passthrough optional)
- Health checks & basic metrics (throughput/latency)

### Phase 2 — ConversationState Manager + Profiles (3 days)
- Implement src/core/conversation_state.py (in-memory + optional persistence)
- Update orchestration pipeline to use Task → Plan → Execute phases
- Add profiles in config: development vs production (switches providers)

### Phase 3 — Provider & Tool Registry (3 days)
- Create src/core/registry.py to load providers & tools from plugins
- Add metadata schema for plugins (name, version, capabilities)
- Move existing providers into registry-compatible modules

### Phase 4 — Centralized Observability + SRE Analytics (5 days)
- Deploy Observability stack (Prometheus, Tempo, Loki, Grafana) or connect to existing SRE Analytics
- Update apps to export OpenTelemetry spans, Prometheus metrics, structured logs
- Create Grafana dashboards for provider latency, fallback rates, cache hit rates, GPU utilization

### Phase 5 — Validation, A/B & Rollout (4 days)
- Run integration tests & canary deployments
- Canary 5–10% traffic to vLLM
- Compare metrics vs baseline for throughput/latency/cost
- Add rollback plan and monitoring alerts
- Promote to full production after acceptance

## Success Metrics
- **vLLM Throughput:** ≥50 req/min
- **vLLM Latency (p95):** <2s
- **Multi-step Collaboration Success:** ≥99%
- **Observability:** Prometheus/OTEL + Grafana dashboards reporting
- **Config Validation:** Passes pydantic schema
- **Provider Switching:** Zero-downtime

## Total Duration
19 days (approximately 3-4 weeks)

goals.title: Enable Bi-Directional Sync Between Orchestrator Tracker and ChatGPT Context
goals.description:
## Overview
Implement a mechanism to automatically sync updates between the AI Orchestrator's internal project tracker (e.g., MongoDB / Notion / local JSON) and the ChatGPT planning context. The goal is to ensure that when enhancements, goals, or progress updates are added through the Orchestrator interface or API, they are automatically reflected in ChatGPT's context without manual copy-paste.

## Objectives
- Design a lightweight sync layer (API endpoint or webhook) to push structured tracker updates to ChatGPT or a shared context endpoint
- Ensure all key project metadata (project name, change type, summary, status) is included in the sync payload
- Maintain two-way awareness — updates from ChatGPT can also be reflected in the Orchestrator tracker
- Store update logs with timestamps and source (Orchestrator / ChatGPT)

## Deliverables
- `/tracker/sync` API endpoint to receive updates
- Background job or script to POST updates to ChatGPT summary endpoint
- YAML/JSON payload schema for updates
- Documentation (docs/TRACKER_SYNC.md) describing the sync process and authentication

## Acceptance Criteria
- ✅ Sync occurs automatically when tracker updates are made
- ✅ ChatGPT context reflects new goals or enhancements within 1 minute of update
- ✅ Manual "Sync Now" trigger available in Orchestrator dashboard
- ✅ End-to-end tested with both OpenAI API and Anthropic Claude Code integration

## Priority & Status
- **Priority**: High
- **Status**: Planned
- **Assigned To**: System Integration Team
- **Dependencies**: AI Orchestrator Architecture Delta rollout completion
- **Target Sprint**: Next (following LLM Expansion deployment)
